question: Why did Fred Dretske say you can know an animal in a zoo pen is a zebra, yet not know it is no painted mule?
answer: Because evidence that settles one question need not settle another it implies. Stripes in a zoo pen rule out horses and antelopes, the live alternatives, but look the same on a painted mule. Dretske argued in 1970 that knowledge need not pass along every known implication. The sceptic wins the mule and loses the zebra.
move: Ask which alternatives your evidence actually rules out before claiming all of them.
ask: Which alternative has my evidence never actually ruled out, though I claim to know?
reference: Dretske, Epistemic Operators, Journal of Philosophy 67 (24), 1970, pp. 1007-1023
